subject: general
question: In February 2025, which international organisation signed a strategic partnership with the African Union to boost vaccine manufacturing on the continent?
solution:
The correct answer is __**GAVI – The Vaccine Alliance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In February 2025, **GAVI – The Vaccine Alliance** signed a strategic partnership with the African Union to bolster vaccine manufacturing on the African continent.
 
• This partnership aims to strengthen **local vaccine production** to reduce dependency on imports and enhance Africa’s health security.
 
• It focuses on **equitable access to vaccines** for African nations, ensuring preparedness for future pandemics.
 
• GAVI has been instrumental in providing **immunization support** globally, particularly in low-income countries, since its inception in 2000.
 
• The African Union has been actively pursuing initiatives to enhance vaccine manufacturing capacity, aligning with its **Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Plan for Africa (PMPA).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GAVI – The Vaccine Alliance:**

 
 
• A global public-private partnership created in 2000 to improve access to vaccines in low-income countries.
 
• Supported by entities like the World Health Organization (WHO), UNICEF, the World Bank, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.
 
• Aims to save lives, reduce poverty, and protect against pandemics through immunization.
 
 
 
• **African Union’s Vaccine Initiative:**
 
 
• The African Union (AU) has been working to reduce its reliance on imported vaccines, especially after challenges faced during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• The AU’s **Partnership for African Vaccine Manufacturing (PAVM)** is a critical part of this effort, aiming to produce 60% of Africa’s vaccine needs locally by 2040.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Vaccine Manufacturing in Africa:**
 
 
• Barriers include limited infrastructure, insufficient funding, and lack of technical expertise.
 
• Global partnerships, such as with GAVI, address these challenges through capacity-building initiatives.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Pandemic and Vaccine Distribution:**
 
 
• The pandemic exposed disparities in global vaccine distribution, with many African nations receiving doses late.
 
• Initiatives like this partnership aim to ensure equitable access in future health crises.
